title: Bias Detection via Maximum Subgroup Discrepancy

problem.claim: Bias evaluation requires assessing data quality and AI system outputs.

gap.claim: Classical metrics such as Total Variation and Wasserstein distances can have high sample complexity and fail to meaningfully distinguish distributions in practical scenarios.

contributions.claim: Introduces Maximum Subgroup Discrepancy, a distance based on discrepancies across feature subgroups.
Provides a practical Mixed-Integer Optimization algorithm for evaluating the distance.
Describes a general bias detection framework based on MSD distances.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that MSD has sample complexity linear in the number of features, despite the potentially exponential number of subgroups.
The authors report that MSD is interpretable and provides clearer paths for addressing identified biases.
The authors empirically evaluate MSD against other metrics and demonstrate its reported properties on real-world datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Bias evaluation is presented as fundamental to trustworthy AI.
Classical distribution distances may be too sample-inefficient for practical bias evaluation.
The paper introduces MSD, evaluates it with MIO, and frames it around subgroup discrepancies.
The authors report comparisons with other metrics and evaluations on real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: The proposed distance evaluates discrepancies across feature subgroups.

interpretation.claim: Subgroup-oriented evaluation may expose biases that aggregate distribution distances overlook.

application.claim: Use subgroup-level discrepancy analysis when evaluating distributional bias in structured data.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which subgroup definitions, data types, or application settings are required.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal definition of MSD.
The abstract does not provide quantitative empirical results or datasets.
The abstract does not detail the MIO formulation or computational scalability.
